6    Q.    Please state your name and business address.

7    A.    My name is J Luebbert and I am employed by the Missouri Public Service

8    Commission as the Manager of the Tariff/Rate Design department of the Commission

9    Staff. My business address is 200 Madison Street, Jefferson City, Missouri 65101.

10   A list of cases that I have participated in before the Commission are attached as

11   Schedule JL-d1.

12   Q.    What is the purpose of your direct testimony?

13   A.    My direct testimony will describe the estimated Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”)

14   transmission related expenses that may be expected from new or increased load from

15   new customers. Generally, the expenses are separated into energy-based charges and

16   demand-based charges in accordance with the SPP assessment of transmission costs.

17   Staff witness Sarah Lange includes the aggregated energy rates and demand rates in

18   Staff’s revenue plug amount to net expenses from revenues.

19   Q.    Do the estimated rates account for energy expense for serving load through SPP’s

20   Integrated Marketplace or additional capacity costs to meet SPP resource adequacy

21   requirements?




                                            Page 1
      Direct Testimony of
     J Luebbert
1    A.       No. The estimated rates that I provide only account for incremental SPP

2    transmission expense related to incremental load.

3    Q.       What SPP transmission rates did you utilize to quantify the rate for

4    energy components?

5    A.       For energy components, I utilized the rates included in SPP’s Open Access

6    Transmission Tariff (“OATT”) price matrix 1 for the following rate schedules:

7         •   Schedule 1-A2: Transmission Congestion Rights Administrative Service

8         •   Schedule 1-A3: Integrated Marketplace Clearing Administrative Service

9         •   Schedule 1-A4: Integrated Marketplace Facilitation Administrative Service

10        •   Schedule 12: FERC Assessment Charge


11   Q.       What SPP transmission expenses did you utilize to quantify the rate for

12   demand components?

13   A.       For demand components, I utilized the rates included in SPP’s Open Access

14   Transmission Tariff (“OATT”) price matrix for Schedule 1-A1 (Transmission Administrative

15   Service) and the following rates derived from SPP Revenue Requirement and Rates file for

16   May 2026 2 in accordance with the OATT:

17        •   Schedule 1: System Control and Dispatch Service (Network Integration

18            Transmission Service)




     1
      https://opsportal.spp.org/PriceMatrix
     2
      https://www.spp.org/Documents/76683/RRR%20For%20Bills%20May%202026%20Revenue%20Requir
     ements%20and%20Rates.xlsx


                                               Page 2
      Direct Testimony of
     J Luebbert
1         •   Addendum 1 to Schedule 1: Tariff Administration Services (Allocation of Through

2             and Out Service)

3         •   Schedule 9: Revenues related to network integrated transmission (Zonal Annual

4             Transmission Revenue Requirement)

5         •   Schedule 11: Revenues related to the base plan transmission upgrades (Region
6             Wide Schedule 11 Point-to-Point Rate)
7

8    Q.       Will   the   actual   expenses    incurred   correspond    precisely   with   the

9    estimated expenses?

10   A.       No, many of the demand based expenses are variable, and based upon the load

11   ratio share of all SPP entities. Furthermore, I estimated the expense conservatively

12   assuming the monthly demand coincided with the SPP hour of determination. Changing

13   load from other entities, investment in the transmission system, and changes from the

14   limited information provided in this case on load projections will all impact the realized

15   SPP transmission expense.

16   Q.       Do any of the rates used in Staff’s estimation account for the impact of day-ahead

17   forecasts and real-time operations of a given customer?

18   A.       No. While Staff recognizes that there is a potential expense associated with the

19   interaction of day-ahead and real-time, Staff is unable to quantify the impact given

20   current information.

21   Q.       On a $/kW basis, what is the average amount of transmission expense that varies

22   based on EMM’s demand?

23   A.       For each month, that amount is $3.4058 per kW.



                                                Page 3
     Direct Testimony of
    J Luebbert
1   Q.    On a $/kWh basis, what is the average amount of transmission expense that varies

2   based on EMM’s load?

3   A.    That amount is $0.000219 per kWh.

4   Q.    Does this conclude your testimony?

5   A.    Yes.




                                           Page 4
                               Credentials and Background of
                                         J Luebbert
       I have a Bachelor of Science degree in Biological Engineering from the University of

Missouri. My work experience prior to becoming of member of the Missouri Public Service

Commission Staff includes three years of regulatory work for the Missouri Department of

Natural Resources.


       I am currently employed as the manager of the Tariff/Rate Design Department of the

Industry Analysis Division of the Missouri Public Service Commission Staff. Prior to holding my

current position, I was employed as Case Manager of the Commission Staff Division, Associate

Engineer of the Engineering Analysis Department of the Industry Analysis Division, and as a

Utility Engineering Specialist III in the Energy Resources Department of the Commission Staff

Division. I have been employed at the Missouri Public Service Commission since March 2016 and

am responsible for preparing staff recommendations and ensuring that Staff presents

recommendations in a neutral, independent manner to inform the Commission of Staff’s position

and possible alternatives.
